kevin: Heads-up — after enabling FP8 kernels on H100 cluster-3 we see tail latency spikes and occasional request failures under sustained 400 qps. Profiling shows kernel-selection oscillation between fp8_mha and int8_mha. Repro steps below. cc @maria @yun

maria: interesting. do you see this only when batch sizes grow? could be batch scheduler + KV eviction race. :thinking:

yun: attaching perf summary from tonight's run: https://internal/redwood/perf/2001234567 (private). gist: p50 ~10ms fp8, p95 jumped 2x, p99 had timeouts. traces show frequent fallback to int8 on the same request.

kevin: repro (short): `TE_CONFIG=fp8 ENABLE_FP8=1 ./run_infer.sh --model redwood-v2 --qps 400 --seq 2048` logs in /tmp/fp8-test.log. grep shows `kernel_choice: fp8_mha -> int8_mha (evict_kv)` ~ every 30s

sam: can you paste the small trace snippet? also what's KV cache hit rate?

kevin: paste snippet: ```[2026-03-17T22:14:33Z] req=435 kernel_choice=fp8_mha reason=overflow_kv_cache fallback=int8_mha latency=156ms
[2026-03-17T22:14:33Z] kv_cache_evicted=1 kv_hit_rate=0.62 batches_in_flight=18```

maria: that's the pattern I've seen — when batches pile up, TE switches kernels because fp8's kernel needs different scratch memory layout. scheduler queues + KV eviction create transient memory pressure.

yun: microbench results i ran locally: single-request fp8 ~1.8x faster than int8 when seq<512. under batch=16, tail fp8 latency increases 1.6x compared to int8 due to repeated kernel reallocation. quick numbers: fp8 p99=210ms, int8 p99=120ms.

sam: immediate mitigation: add hysteresis to kernel selector to avoid flip-flops. prefer staying on same kernel for N seconds unless sustained metric breach. :+1:

maria: agreed. proposed selector config: ```selector.hysteresis_ms=5000
selector.switch_threshold=0.15
selector.min_stability_windows=3
kernel.preference=["fp8_mha","int8_mha","int4_mha"]```

kevin: can we also tweak KV cache eviction policy? increase soft cap, or delay eviction when batches_in_flight>12.

yun: tried raising soft cap by 20% earlier — reduced evictions but increased memory pressure; combined with selector hysteresis gives stable tails in canary runs.

sam: i'll open a canary with `redwood-runtime:canary/kernel-hysteresis` and tune on cluster-3 low-traffic first. plan: 1) deploy canary 2) enable hysteresis 3) run qps 200->400 ramp 4) monitor p99 + kv_evictions

kevin: sounds good. please tag me. also add a diagnostic metric `kernel_switch_rate`.

infra-bot: deploy task queued: redwood-runtime:canary/kernel-hysteresis -> cluster-3. CI checks OK :white_check_mark:

maria: once canary looks stable we should add an automatic fallback policy: if kernel_switch_rate>5/min AND kv_evictions>3 in 1m window, force int8 for that route for 5m. :rocket:
